1.contenido: 1. The centenary of the promulgation of the encyclical of my predecessor Leo XIII, of venerated memory, which begins with the words Rerum novarum 1, marks a date of relevant importance in the recent history of the Church and also in my pontificate. It, in fact, has had the privilege of being commemorated, with solemn documents, by the Supreme Pontiffs, from its fortieth anniversary to its ninetieth: it can be said that its historical character has been remembered with other writings that, at the same time, updated it 2.

2.contenido: 2. The present encyclical is situated within the framework of these celebrations to give thanks to God, from whom "every excellent gift and every perfect donation descends" ([+[0]+]), because it has used a document, issued one hundred years ago by the See of Peter, which was to give so many benefits to the Church and the world and spread so much light. The commemoration here refers to the Leonian encyclical and also to the encyclicals and other writings of my predecessors, which have contributed to making it current and operational over time, thus constituting what was to be called "social doctrine", "social teaching" or also "social teaching" of the Church.

3.contenido: 3. I now want to propose a "re-reading" of the Leonian encyclical, inviting us to "take a retrospective look" at its own text, to discover once again the richness of the fundamental principles formulated in it, in order to solve the workers' question. I also invite you to "look around," at the "new things" that surround us and in which, so to speak, we find ourselves immersed, so different from the "new things" that characterized the last decade of the last century. Finally, I invite you to "look to the future", when we already glimpse the third millennium of the Christian era, full of unknowns, but also of promises. Unknowns and promises that challenge our imagination and creativity, while stimulating our responsibility, as disciples of the only teacher, Christ ([+[0]+]), with a view to indicating the way to proclaim the truth and communicate the life that is himself ([+[1]+]).

4.contenido: 4. At the end of the last century the Church found itself faced with a historical process, present for some time, but which was then reaching its peak. The determining factor of this process was a set of radical changes that occurred in the political, economic and social field, and even in the scientific and technical field, apart from the multiple influence of the dominant ideologies. The result of all these changes had been, in the political field, a new conception of society, of the State and, as a consequence, of authority. A traditional society was becoming extinct, while another began to form, loaded with the hope of new freedoms, but at the same time with the dangers of new forms of injustice and slavery.

5.contenido: 5. The “new things” that the Pope had before him were by no means all positive. On the contrary, the first paragraph of the encyclical describes the "new things" that gave it its name in harsh words: "Awakened by the desire for novelties that has been agitating the people for some time now, it was to be expected that the desire to change everything would one day move from the field of politics to the adjacent field of the economy. Indeed, the advances of industry and professions, which are taking new paths; the change that has occurred in the mutual relations between employers and workers; the accumulation of wealth in the hands of a few and the poverty of the vast majority; The greater self-confidence of the workers and the closer cohesion among them, together with the relaxation of morale, have determined the approach to the conflict" 8.

6.contenido: 6. With the purpose of clarifying the conflict that had been created between capital and labor, Leo XIII defended the fundamental rights of workers. Hence, the key to reading the Leonian text is the dignity of the worker as such and, for this reason, the dignity of work, defined as "the activity ordered to provide for the needs of life, and specifically its conservation"12. The Pontiff qualifies the work as "personal", since "the active force is inherent to the person and totally specific to the one who develops it and for whose benefit it has been given"13. Work belongs, therefore, to the vocation of every person; What's more, man expresses himself and fulfills himself through his work activity. At the same time, work has a social dimension, due to its intimate relationship either with the family or with the common good, "because it can be truthfully stated that the work of workers is what produces the wealth of the States"14. All this has been collected and developed in my encyclical Laborem exercens 15.

7.contenido: 7. In close relation to the right of property, the encyclical of Leo XIII also affirms other rights, as proper and inalienable of the human person. Among these, given the space that the Pope dedicates to it and the importance he attributes to it, the "natural right of man" to form private associations stands out; which means above all the right to create professional associations of businessmen and workers, or of workers only 19. This is the reason why the Church defends and approves the creation of the so-called unions, certainly not because of ideological prejudices, nor because of giving in to a class mentality, but because it is precisely a "natural right" of the human being and, therefore, prior to their integration into political society. Indeed, "the State cannot prohibit their formation," because "the State must protect natural rights, not destroy them. By prohibiting such associations, he would contradict himself»20.

8.contenido: 8. Next the Pope states another right of the worker as a person. This is the right to a "fair salary", which cannot be left "to free agreement between the parties, since, according to this, once the agreed salary has been paid, it seems as if the employer had already fulfilled his duty and owed nothing more"23. The State, it was said then, does not have the power to intervene in the determination of these contracts, but rather to ensure compliance with what has been explicitly agreed upon. Such a conception of relations between employers and workers, purely pragmatic and inspired by rigorous individualism, is severely criticized in the encyclical as contrary to the double nature of work, as a personal and necessary factor. If work, insofar as it is personal, belongs to the availability that each person has of their own faculties and energies, insofar as it is necessary it is regulated by the serious obligation that each person has to "preserve his life"; hence "the necessary consequence," the Pope concludes, "of the right to seek what serves to sustain one's life, which for poor people is reduced to the salary earned with their own work"24.

9.contenido: 9. Always referring to the worker condition, to these rights Leo XIII adds another, which I consider necessary to remember due to its importance: the right to freely fulfill one's religious duties. The Pope proclaims it in the context of the other rights and duties of workers, despite the general climate that, even in his time, considered certain issues as pertinent exclusively to the private sphere. He ratifies the need for festive rest, so that man may elevate his thoughts towards the goods above and pay due worship to the divine majesty 28. No one can deprive man of this right, based on a commandment: "it is not permissible for anyone to violate with impunity the dignity of man, whom God himself disposes of with great respect." Consequently, the State must ensure the worker the exercise of this freedom 29.

10.contenido: 10. Another important note, rich in lessons for our days, is the conception of the relations between the State and citizens. Rerum Novarum criticizes the two social and economic systems: socialism and liberalism. The initial part is dedicated to the first, in which the right to private property is reaffirmed; A special section is not dedicated to the second, but - and this deserves a lot of attention - criticism is reserved for it, when addressing the issue of the duties of the State 32, which cannot be limited to "favoring one part of the citizens", that is, the rich and prosperous, and "neglecting the other", which undoubtedly represents the vast majority of the social body; Otherwise, justice is violated, which mandates that each person be given what is theirs. However, "in the protection of these individual rights, special consideration must be given to the weak and poor. The rich class, already powerful in itself, has less need to be protected by public powers; On the other hand, the proletarian class, lacking its own support, has a specific need to seek it in the protection of the State. Therefore, it is to the workers, mostly weak and needy, that the State must direct its preferences and care"33.

11.contenido: 11. Rereading that encyclical, in the light of contemporary realities, allows us to appreciate the constant concern and dedication of the Church for those people who are the object of predilection on the part of Jesus, our Lord. The content of the text is an excellent testimony of the continuity, within the Church, of what is now called "preferential option for the poor"; option that in the Sollicitudo rei socialis is defined as a "special form of primacy in the exercise of Christian charity"36. The encyclical on the "worker question" is, then, an encyclical about the poor and about the terrible condition to which the new and often violent process of industrialization had reduced great multitudes. Also today, in much of the world, similar processes of economic, social and political transformation give rise to the same evils.

12.contenido: 12. The commemoration of Rerum Novarum would not be appropriate without taking a look at the current situation. Due to its content, the document lends itself to such consideration, since its historical framework and the forecasts outlined in it turn out to be surprisingly fair, in light of what happened later.

13.contenido: 13. Delving now into this reflection and referring to what has already been said in the encyclicals Laborem exercens and Sollicitudo rei socialis, we must add here that the fundamental error of socialism is of an anthropological nature. Indeed, it considers every man as a simple element and a molecule of the social organism, so that the good of the individual is subordinated to the functioning of the economic-social mechanism. On the other hand, he considers that this same good can be achieved outside of his autonomous option, of his assumed responsibility, unique and exclusive, for good or evil. Man is thus reduced to a series of social relations, disappearing the concept of the person as an autonomous subject of moral decision, who is the one who builds the social order, through such decision. From this erroneous conception of the person comes the distortion of law, which defines the scope of the exercise of freedom, and the opposition to private property. Man, in fact, when he lacks something that he can call "his" and has no possibility of earning to live on his own initiative, becomes dependent on the social machine and those who control it, which creates greater difficulties for him to recognize his dignity as a person and hinders his path to the constitution of an authentic human community.

14.contenido: 14. From the same atheistic root also arises the choice of the means of action typical of socialism, condemned in Rerum Novarum. It's about class struggle. The Pope certainly does not intend to condemn each and every form of social conflict. The Church knows very well that, throughout history, conflicts of interest between various social groups inevitably arise and that Christians must often speak out against them with coherence and decision. Furthermore, the encyclical Laborem exercens has clearly recognized the positive role of conflict when it is configured as a "struggle for social justice"41. Already in Quadragesimo anno it was said: "Indeed, when the class struggle abstains from acts of violence and mutual hatred, it gradually transforms into an honest discussion, founded on the search for justice"42.

15.contenido: 15. Rerum novarum opposes the stateization of the means of production, which would reduce every citizen to a "cog" in the gears of the state machine. With no less decisiveness he criticizes a conception of the State that leaves the sphere of the economy totally outside its own field of interest and action. There is certainly a legitimate sphere of autonomy of economic activity, where the State should not intervene. It is up to the latter, however, to determine the legal framework within which economic relations are developed and thus safeguard the fundamental conditions of a free economy, which presupposes a certain equality between the parties, lest one of them so much surpasses the other in power that it can practically reduce it to slavery 43.

16.contenido: 16. The reforms were carried out in part by the States; but in the fight to achieve them the action of the labor movement played an important role. Born as a reaction of moral conscience against situations of injustice and harm, it developed a vast union, reformist activity, far from the fog of ideology and closer to the daily needs of workers. In this area, their efforts frequently joined those of Christians to achieve better living conditions for workers. Later, this Movement was dominated, in a certain way, precisely by the Marxist ideology against which Rerum Novarum was directed.

17.contenido: 17. Reading the encyclical in relation to all the rich Leonian teaching 47, one notices that, deep down, it is pointing out the consequences of a more far-reaching error in the economic-social field. It is the error that, as has already been said, consists of a conception of human freedom that separates it from obedience to the truth and, therefore, also from the duty to respect the rights of other men. The content of freedom is then transformed into self-love, with contempt for God and neighbor; love that leads to the unlimited strengthening of one's own interest and that does not allow itself to be limited by any obligation of justice 48.

18.contenido: 18. It is true that since 1945 the guns have been silent on the European continent; However, true peace - let us remember - is not the result of military victory, but something that implies overcoming the causes of war and authentic reconciliation between peoples. For many years, however, there has been a situation in Europe and the world of non-war, rather than genuine peace. Half of the continent falls under the rule of the communist dictatorship, while the other half organizes to defend itself against such danger. Many people lose the power to govern themselves, locked in the oppressive confines of an empire, while attempts are made to destroy their historical memory and the secular roots of their culture. As a consequence of this violent division, enormous masses of men are forced to abandon their land and forcibly deported.

19.contenido: 19. At the end of the Second World War, this process is still being formed in consciences; but the fact that is offered to view is the extension of communist totalitarianism to more than half of Europe and a large part of the world. The war, which should have restored freedom and restored the rights of nations, is concluded without having achieved these ends; Furthermore, it is concluded in a way that is openly contradictory for many peoples, especially for those who had suffered the most. It can be said that the situation created has given rise to various responses.

20.contenido: 20. During the same period, a grandiose process of "decolonization" was developing, by virtue of which numerous countries achieved or regained independence and the right to freely dispose of themselves. However, with the formal reconquest of their state sovereignty, these countries in many cases are just beginning the path of building authentic independence. Indeed, decisive sectors of the economy are still in the hands of large foreign companies, which do not accept a lasting commitment that links them to the development of the country that receives them. Sometimes, political life is also subject to the control of foreign forces, while tribal groups sometimes coexist within the borders of the State, not yet amalgamated into an authentic national community. Furthermore, there is a lack of a core of competent professionals capable of making the administrative apparatus of the State function honestly and regularly, and there is also a lack of teams of specialized people for efficient and responsible management of the economy.

21.contenido: 21. It must be remembered, finally, that after the Second World War, and partly as a reaction to its horrors, a more lively feeling for human rights has spread, which has been recognized in various international documents 52, and in the development, one could say, of a new "law of nations", to which the Holy See has given a constant contribution. The key piece of this evolution has been the United Nations Organization. Not only has awareness of the rights of individuals grown, but also that of the rights of nations, while there is greater awareness of the need to act to correct the serious imbalances that exist between the various geographical areas of the world that, in a certain sense, have moved the center of the social issue from the national to the international level 53.

22.contenido: 22. Starting from the world situation just described, and already explained at length in the encyclical Sollicitudo rei socialis, we understand the unexpected and promising scope of the events that have occurred in recent years. Its culmination is certainly what happened in 1989 in the countries of central and eastern Europe; but they cover a broader arc of time and geographical horizon. Throughout the eighties, certain dictatorial and oppressive regimes gradually fell in some countries in Latin America, and even in Africa and Asia; In other cases, a difficult but fruitful transition path begins towards fairer political forms with greater participation. Important and even decisive help has been given by the Church, with its commitment to the defense and promotion of human rights. In intensely ideologized environments, where partisan positions obscured the awareness of common human dignity, the Church has affirmed with simplicity and energy that every man – whatever his personal convictions – carries within him the image of God and, therefore, deserves respect. The vast majority of the people have frequently identified themselves in this statement, which has led them to seek forms of struggle and political solutions that are more respectful of the dignity of the human person.

23.contenido: 23. Among the numerous factors in the fall of oppressive regimes, some deserve to be remembered in a special way. The decisive factor that has set the changes in motion is without a doubt the violation of worker rights. It cannot be forgotten that the fundamental crisis of the systems that claim to be an expression of the government and, what is more, of the dictatorship of the proletariat begins with the great revolts that took place in Poland in the name of solidarity. It is the multitudes of workers who disavow the ideology, which claims to be their voice; They are the ones who find and as if they rediscover expressions and principles of the social doctrine of the Church, starting from the lived and difficult experience of work and oppression.

24.contenido: 24. The second crisis factor is, in fact, the inefficiency of the economic system, which should not be considered as a purely technical problem, but rather as a consequence of the violation of the human rights to initiative, property and freedom in the sector of the economy. To this aspect we must secondly associate the cultural and national dimensions. It is not possible to understand man, considering him unilaterally from the sector of the economy, nor is it possible to define him simply based on his membership in a social class. Man is understood more exhaustively if he is seen in the sphere of culture through language, history and the attitudes he assumes towards the fundamental events of existence, such as being born, loving, working, dying. The central point of every culture is the attitude that man assumes before the greatest mystery: the mystery of God. The cultures of different nations are, in essence, so many different ways of asking the question about the meaning of personal existence. When this question is eliminated, the culture and moral life of nations are corrupted. For this reason, the fight for the defense of labor has spontaneously joined the fight for culture and national rights.

25.contenido: 25. The events of 1989 offer an example of the success of the will to negotiate and the evangelical spirit against an adversary determined not to allow itself to be conditioned by moral principles: they are a warning to those who, in the name of political realism, want to eliminate law and morality from the arena of politics. Certainly the struggle that led to the changes of 1989 has required lucidity, moderation, suffering and sacrifices; In a certain sense, it was born from prayer and would have been unthinkable without unlimited trust in God, Lord of history, who holds the hearts of men in his hands. By uniting one's own suffering for truth and freedom to that of Christ on the cross, this is how man can perform the miracle of peace and put himself in a position to navigate the sometimes narrow path between the meanness that gives way to evil and the violence that, illusorily believing to combat it, aggravates it.

26.contenido: 26. The events of 1989 took place mainly in the countries of Eastern and Central Europe; However, they are of universal importance, since they give rise to positive and negative consequences that affect the entire human family. Such consequences do not occur in a mechanical or fatalistic way, but rather are opportunities offered to human freedom to collaborate with the merciful plan of God that acts in history.

27.contenido: 27. The second consequence affects the people of Europe. In the years when communism dominated, and also before, many individual and social, regional and national injustices were committed; Many hatreds and resentments accumulated. And the danger remains real that they will explode again, after the fall of the dictatorship, causing serious conflicts and deaths, if the moral tension and conscious firmness in bearing witness to the truth, which have animated the efforts of the past, decrease. It is to be hoped that hatred and violence do not triumph in the hearts, especially of those who fight for justice, but that the spirit of peace and forgiveness grows in everyone.

28.contenido: 28. For some European countries, in a certain sense, the true postwar period now begins. The radical restructuring of the economies, until yesterday collectivized, entails problems and sacrifices, comparable to those that the Western countries of the continent had to impose themselves for their reconstruction after the second world conflict. It is fair that in the present difficulties the ex-communist countries be helped by the solidarity efforts of other nations: obviously, they must be the first architects of their own development; but they must be given a reasonable opportunity to do so, and this cannot be achieved without the help of other countries. Furthermore, the current conditions of difficulty and hardship are the consequence of a historical process, of which ex-communist countries have sometimes been the object and not the subject; Therefore, if they find themselves in these conditions it is not by their own choice or because of errors committed, but as a consequence of tragic historical events imposed by violence, which have prevented them from continuing along the path of economic and civil development.

29.contenido: 29. Finally, development should not be understood in an exclusively economic manner, but rather under a comprehensive human dimension 61. It is not only about elevating all peoples to the level enjoyed today by the richest countries, but about founding a more dignified life on solidarity work, effectively making the dignity and creativity of every person grow, their ability to respond to their own vocation and, therefore, to the call of God. The culminating point of development entails the exercise of the right-duty to seek God, know Him and live according to such knowledge 62. In totalitarian and authoritarian regimes the principle of the primacy of force over reason has been extreme. Man has been forced to suffer a conception of reality imposed by force, and not achieved through the effort of one's own reason and the exercise of one's own freedom. We must reverse the terms of that principle and fully recognize the rights of human conscience, linked only to natural and revealed truth. The primary foundation of any truly free political order lies in the recognition of these rights 63. It is important to reaffirm this principle for several reasons:

30.contenido: 30. In Rerum Novarum, Leo Likewise, the Church teaches that the ownership of goods is not an absolute right, since its own limitation is inscribed in its nature as a human right.

31.contenido: 31. Rereading these teachings on the right to property and the common destiny of goods in relation to our time, the question can be raised about the origin of the goods that sustain man's life, that satisfy his needs and are the object of his rights.

32.contenido: 32. There is another form of property, specifically in our time, which is of no less importance than that of land: it is the property of knowledge, technology and knowledge. The wealth of industrialized nations is based on this type of property, much more than on natural resources.

33.contenido: 33. However, it is necessary to discover and present the risks and problems related to this type of process. In fact, today many men, perhaps the vast majority, do not have the means that allow them to enter in an effective and humanly dignified manner into a business system, where work occupies a truly central position. They do not have the possibility of acquiring basic knowledge that helps them express their creativity and develop their abilities. They do not manage to enter the network of knowledge and intercommunications that would allow them to see their qualities appreciated and used. They, although not properly exploited, are widely marginalized and economic development is carried out, so to speak, beyond their reach, limiting even the already reduced spaces of their former subsistence economies. These men, powerless to resist the competition of goods produced with new methods and that satisfy needs that they previously used to face with their traditional organizational forms, dazzled by the splendor of an ostentatious opulence, unattainable for them, constrained in turn by necessity, these men form true agglomerations in the cities of the Third World, where they often find themselves culturally uprooted, in the midst of situations of violence and without the possibility of integration. In fact, their dignity is not recognized and, sometimes, attempts are made to eliminate them from history through coercive forms of demographic control, contrary to human dignity.

34.contenido: 34. It gives the impression that, both at the level of nations and international relations, the free market is the most effective instrument to allocate resources and respond effectively to needs. However, this applies only to those needs that are "solvent", with purchasing power, and for those resources that are "saleable", that is, capable of reaching a convenient price. But there are numerous human needs that have no outlet in the market. It is a strict duty of justice and truth to prevent fundamental human needs from going unsatisfied and the men oppressed by them from perishing. Furthermore, these needy men must be helped to obtain knowledge, to enter the circle of interrelationships, to develop their skills in order to better value their abilities and resources. Above the logic of exchanges based on parameters and their just forms, there is something that is due to man because he is a man, by virtue of his eminent dignity. This something due inseparably entails the possibility of surviving and actively participating in the common good of humanity.

35.contenido: 35. A vast and fruitful field of action and struggle opens up here, in the name of justice, for unions and other workers' organizations, which defend their rights and protect their person, while performing an essential function of a cultural nature, to make them participate in a more full and dignified manner in the life of the nation and help them on the path of development.

36.contenido: 36. It is now appropriate to direct attention to the specific problems and threats that arise within the most advanced economies and in relation to their peculiar characteristics. In the preceding phases of development, man has always lived conditioned under the weight of necessity. The necessary things were few, already fixed in some way by the objective structures of their corporeal constitution, and economic activity was aimed at satisfying them. It is clear, however, that today the problem is not only to offer a sufficient quantity of goods, but to respond to a demand for quality: quality of the merchandise that is produced and consumed; quality of the services enjoyed; quality of the environment and life in general.

37.contenido: 37. Also worrying, along with the problem of consumerism and strictly linked to it, is the ecological issue. Man, driven by the desire to have and enjoy, more than to be and grow, consumes the earth's resources and his own life in an excessive and disorderly manner. At the root of the senseless destruction of the natural environment is an anthropological error, unfortunately widespread in our time. Man, who discovers his capacity to transform and, in a certain sense, to "create" the world with his own work, forgets that this always develops on the basis of the first and original gift of things by God. He believes that he can arbitrarily dispose of the earth, subjecting it without reservation to his will as if it did not have its own physiognomy and a previous destiny given by God, and that man can certainly develop, but that he must not betray. Instead of playing his role as God's collaborator in the work of creation, man supplants God and thereby provokes the rebellion of nature, which is rather tyrannized than governed by him 76.

38.contenido: 38. In addition to the irrational destruction of the natural environment, we must remember here the even more serious destruction of the human environment, to which, however, the necessary attention is far from being paid. While we rightly concern ourselves, although much less than necessary, with preserving the natural "habitats" of the various animal species threatened with extinction, because we realize that each of them makes its own contribution to the general balance of the earth, we make very little effort to safeguard the moral conditions of an authentic "human ecology." Not only has the earth been given by God to man, who must use it respecting the original intention that it is a good, according to which it has been given to him; Even man is a gift from God to himself and, therefore, he must respect the natural and moral structure with which he has been endowed. It is necessary to mention in this context the serious problems of modern urbanization, the need for urban planning concerned with people's lives, as well as due attention to a "social ecology" of work.

39.contenido: 39. The first fundamental structure in favor of "human ecology" is the family, within which man receives the first notions about truth and goodness; learn what it means to love and be loved, and therefore what it means specifically to be a person. Here we understand the family founded on marriage, in which the reciprocal gift of self by the man and the woman creates a living environment in which the child can be born and develop his or her potential, become aware of his or her dignity and prepare to face his or her unique and unrepeatable destiny. On the other hand, it often happens that man feels discouraged from realizing the authentic conditions of human reproduction and is induced to consider his own life and himself as a set of sensations to be experienced rather than as a work to be performed. From this arises a lack of freedom that makes one renounce the commitment to bond in a stable manner with another person and have children, or it moves one to consider them as one of many "things" that it is possible to have or not have, according to one's own tastes, and that are presented as other options.

40.contenido: 40. It is the duty of the State to provide for the defense and protection of collective goods, such as the natural environment and the human environment, whose safeguard cannot be assured by simple market mechanisms. Just as in times of old capitalism the State had the duty to defend fundamental labor rights, so now with the new capitalism the State and society have the duty to defend collective goods which, among other things, constitute the only framework within which it is possible for each person to legitimately achieve their individual goals.

41.contenido: 41. Marxism has criticized bourgeois and capitalist societies, reproaching them for the commercialization and alienation of human existence. Certainly, this reproach is based on a mistaken and inadequate conception of alienation, according to which it depends solely on the sphere of production and property relations, that is, attributing to it a materialist foundation and, furthermore, denying the legitimacy and positivity of market relations even in their own sphere. Marxism thus ends up affirming that only in a collectivist society could alienation be eradicated. Now, the historical experience of socialist countries has sadly demonstrated that collectivism does not end alienation, but rather increases it, by adding to it the scarcity of necessary things and economic inefficiency.

42.contenido: 42. Returning now to the initial question, can we perhaps say that, after the failure of communism, the winning system is capitalism, and that the efforts of the countries trying to rebuild their economy and society are directed towards it? Is this perhaps the model that needs to be proposed to Third World countries that seek the path to true economic and civil progress?

43.contenido: 43. The Church has no models to propose. Real and truly effective models can only arise from the various historical situations, thanks to the efforts of all those responsible who face the specific problems in all their social, economic, political and cultural aspects that are related to each other 84. For this objective the Church offers, as ideal and indispensable guidance, its own social doctrine, which âas has been saidâ recognizes the positivity of the market and the company, but at the same time indicates that they must be oriented towards the common good. This doctrine also recognizes the legitimacy of workers' efforts to achieve full respect for their dignity and broader spaces for participation in the life of the company, so that, even when working together with others and under the direction of others, they can consider in a certain sense that they are "working on something of their own" 85, by exercising their intelligence and freedom.

44.contenido: 44. Leo social of man, which requires adequate legislation to protect the freedom of all. In this regard, it is preferable that a power be balanced by other powers and other spheres of competence, which keep it within its fair limit. This is the principle of the "Rule of Law", in which the law and not the arbitrary will of men is sovereign.

45.contenido: 45. The culture and praxis of totalitarianism also entail the denial of the Church. The State, or the party, which believes it can achieve absolute good in history and stands above all values, cannot tolerate the maintenance of an objective criterion of good and evil, above the will of the rulers and which, in certain circumstances, can be used to judge their behavior. This explains why totalitarianism tries to destroy the Church or, at least, subjugate it, turning it into an instrument of its own ideological apparatus 92.

46.contenido: 46. The Church appreciates the system of democracy, to the extent that it ensures the participation of citizens in political options and guarantees the governed the possibility of choosing and controlling their own rulers, or of replacing them in a timely manner in a peaceful manner 93. For this reason, it cannot favor the formation of restricted ruling groups that, for particular interests or ideological reasons, usurp the power of the State.

47.contenido: 47. After the fall of communist totalitarianism and many other totalitarian and "national security" regimes, we today witness the predominance, not without contrasts, of the democratic ideal together with a lively attention and concern for human rights. But, precisely for this reason, it is necessary that the peoples who are reforming their laws give democracy an authentic and solid foundation, through the explicit recognition of these rights 96. Among the main ones we must remember: the right to life, of which the right of the child to grow under the mother's heart, after having been conceived, is an integral part; the right to live in a united family and in a moral environment, favorable to the development of one's personality; the right to mature one's own intelligence and one's freedom through the search and knowledge of the truth; the right to participate in work to value the goods of the earth and obtain from it the sustenance of oneself and one's loved ones; the right to freely found a family, to welcome and educate children, making responsible use of one's sexuality. Source and synthesis of these rights is, in a certain sense, religious freedom, understood as the right to live in the truth of one's faith and in accordance with the transcendent dignity of one's own person 97.

48.contenido: 48. These general considerations are also reflected on the role of the State in the economic sector. Economic activity, particularly the market economy, cannot develop in the midst of an institutional, legal and political vacuum. On the contrary, it implies a security that guarantees individual freedom and property, as well as a stable monetary system and efficient public services. The first responsibility of the State is, therefore, to guarantee this security, so that those who work and produce can enjoy the fruits of their work and, therefore, feel encouraged to do it efficiently and honestly. The lack of security, together with the corruption of public powers and the proliferation of improper sources of enrichment and easy profits, based on illegal or purely speculative activities, is one of the main obstacles to development and the economic order.

49.contenido: 49. In this field the Church, faithful to the mandate of Christ, its Founder, has always been present with its works, which tend to offer man in need material support that does not humiliate him or reduce him to being only an object of assistance, but rather helps him get out of his precarious situation, promoting his dignity as a person. Thank God, it must be said that active charity has never been extinguished in the Church and, what's more, it currently has a multiform and consoling increase. In this regard, the phenomenon of volunteerism is worthy of special mention, which the Church favors and promotes, requesting the collaboration of everyone to support and encourage it in its initiatives.

50.contenido: 50. This open search for truth, which is renewed each generation, characterizes the culture of the nation. Indeed, the heritage of inherited and acquired values ​​is frequently the object of contestation by young people. Answering, on the other hand, does not necessarily mean destroying or rejecting a priori, but above all it means putting it to the test in one's own life and, after this existential verification, making those values ​​more alive, current and personal, discerning what is valid in tradition with respect to falsehoods and errors or obsolete forms, which can be replaced by others more in line with the times.

51.contenido: 51. All human activity takes place within a culture and has a reciprocal relationship with it. For an adequate formation of this culture, the direct participation of all men is required, who develops in it their creativity, their intelligence, their knowledge of the world and of other men. To her he also dedicates his capacity for self-control, personal sacrifice, solidarity and availability to promote the common good. For this reason, the first and most important work is carried out in the heart of man, and the way in which he commits to building his own future depends on the conception he has of himself and his destiny. It is at this level where the specific and decisive contribution of the Church in favor of true culture takes place. It promotes the level of human behavior that favors the culture of peace against models that nullify man in the masses, ignore the role of his creativity and freedom and place the greatness of man in his gifts for conflict and war. The Church carries out this service by preaching the truth about the creation of the world, which God has placed in the hands of men so that they may make it fruitful and more perfect with their work, and by preaching the truth about the Redemption, through which the Son of God has saved all men and at the same time has united them among themselves, making them responsible for each other. Holy Scripture continually speaks to us about active commitment in favor of our brother and presents us with the demand for a co-responsibility that must encompass all men.

52.contenido: 52. The Pontiffs Benedict XV and his successors have clearly seen this danger 104, and I myself, on the occasion of the recent and dramatic war in the Persian Gulf, have repeated the cry: "Never again war!" No, never again war! It destroys the lives of the innocent, which teaches to kill and also disrupts the lives of those who kill, which leaves behind a sequel of resentment and hatred, and makes it more difficult to find a just solution to the same problems that caused it. Just as within each State the time has finally come when the system of private vengeance and reprisal has been replaced by the rule of law, so it is now urgent that such progress take place in the international Community. We must not forget either that at the root of war there are, in general, real and serious reasons: injustices suffered, frustrations of legitimate aspirations, misery or exploitation of large desperate human masses, who do not see the objective possibility of improving their conditions through peace.

53.contenido: 53. Faced with the misery of the proletariat, Leo In the last hundred years the Church has repeatedly expressed its thoughts, closely following the continuous evolution of the social question, and this has certainly not been done to recover privileges from the past or to impose its own conception. Its sole purpose has been care and responsibility towards man, entrusted to it by Christ himself, towards this man, who, as the Second Vatican Council recalls, is the only creature that God willed for itself and for whom he has his project, that is, participation in eternal salvation. It is not about abstract man, but about real, concrete and historical man: it is about each man, because the mystery of redemption comes to each one, and with each one Christ has been united forever through this mystery 108. From this it follows that the Church cannot abandon man, and that "this man is the first path that the Church must follow in the fulfillment of its mission..., a path traced by Christ himself, a path that immutably leads through the mystery of the incarnation and the redemption»109.

54.contenido: 54. Social doctrine, especially today, looks at man, inserted in the complex web of relationships of modern society. The human sciences and philosophy help to interpret the centrality of man in society and make him capable of better understanding himself, as a "social being." However, only faith fully reveals its true identity, and precisely from it begins the social doctrine of the Church, which, using all the contributions of science and philosophy, proposes to help man on the path of salvation.

55.contenido: 55. The Church knows the "sense of man" thanks to divine Revelation. "To know man, the true man, the integral man, one must know God," said Paul VI, then quoting Saint Catherine of Siena, who in a prayer expressed the same idea: "In the divine nature, eternal Deity, I will know my nature"110.

56.contenido: 56. On the first centenary of this Encyclical, I wish to thank all those who have dedicated themselves to studying, deepening and disseminating Christian social doctrine. For this, the collaboration of local Churches is essential, and I hope that the commemoration will be an occasion for a renewed push for its study, dissemination and application in all areas.

57.contenido: 57. For the Church, the social message of the Gospel should not be considered a theory, but, above all, a foundation and a stimulus for action. Driven by this message, some of the first Christians distributed their goods to the poor, testifying that, despite the diverse social backgrounds, a peaceful and supportive coexistence was possible. With the force of the Gospel, over the centuries, the monks cultivated the lands; religious men and women founded hospitals and asylums for the poor; The brotherhoods, as well as men and women of all social classes, committed themselves to the needy and marginalized, convinced that the words of Christ: "As many times as you do these things to one of the least of my brothers, you have done them to me" ( [+[0]+] ) should not remain a pious wish, but become a concrete commitment of life.

58.contenido: 58. Love for man and, first of all, for the poor, in whom the Church sees Christ, is realized in the promotion of justice. This can never be fully realized if men do not recognize in the needy, who asks for help for their life, not someone who is inconvenient or as if they were a burden, but rather the opportunity for good in itself, the possibility of greater wealth. Only this awareness will give the strength to face the risk and change implicit in any authentic initiative to help another man. In fact, it is not just about giving what is superfluous, but about helping entire peoples âwho are excluded or marginalizedâ€ to enter the circle of economic and human development. This will be possible not only by using the superfluous that our world produces in abundance, but above all by changing lifestyles, production and consumption models, and the consolidated power structures that govern society today. Nor is it a question of destroying instruments of social organization that have given good proof of themselves, but of orienting them according to an adequate conception of the common good with reference to the entire human family. Today the so-called "planetary economy" is already being experienced, a phenomenon that should not be underestimated, because it can create extraordinary opportunities for greater well-being. But every day the need is felt more and more for this growing internationalization of the economy to correspond with adequate valid international control and guidance bodies, which guide the economy itself towards the common good, something that a single State, even if it were the most powerful on earth, is not capable of achieving. In order to achieve this result, it is necessary that coordination between large countries increases and that the interests of the entire great human family are equally represented in international organizations. It is also necessary that when assessing the consequences of their decisions, they always take into consideration the peoples and countries that have little weight in the international market and that, on the other hand, are burdened with a whole series of real and pressing needs that require greater support for adequate development. Undoubtedly, much remains to be done in this field.

59.contenido: 59. Therefore, for justice to be exercised and men's efforts to establish it to be successful, the gift of grace, which comes from God, is necessary. Through it, in collaboration with the freedom of men, the mysterious presence of God in history, which is Providence, is achieved.

60.contenido: 60. When enunciating the principles for the solution of the workers' question, Leo XIII wrote: "The solution of such an arduous problem requires the help and effective cooperation of others"114. He was convinced that the serious problems caused by industrial society could be solved only through collaboration between all forces. This statement has become a permanent element of the social doctrine of the Church, and this explains, among other things, why John XXIII addressed his encyclical on peace to "all men of good will."

61.contenido: 61. It was "the almost servile yoke", at the beginning of industrial society, that forced my predecessor to speak out in defense of man. The Church has remained faithful to this commitment over the past hundred years. Indeed, it has intervened in the turbulent period of class struggle, after the First World War, to defend man from economic exploitation and the tyranny of totalitarian systems. After the Second World War, it has placed the dignity of the person at the center of its social messages, insisting on the universal destination of material goods, on a social order without oppression based on the spirit of collaboration and solidarity. Then, he has continually affirmed that the person and society do not only need these goods, but also spiritual and religious values. Furthermore, realizing more and more that too many men live not in the well-being of the Western world, but in the misery of developing countries and endure a condition that continues to be that of the "almost servile yoke", the Church has felt and continues to feel the obligation to denounce such a reality with complete clarity and frankness, although it knows that its cry will not always be received favorably by everyone.

62.contenido: 62. This encyclical today sought to look to the past, but above all it is oriented to the future. Like Rerum Novarum, it is almost on the threshold of the new century and, with divine help, it intends to prepare its arrival.
